title: The Choir of the Sundered Sea
premise: Astrid Ravensworth, a mercenary whose god fell silent years ago, takes in a feral child who speaks the dead tongue of the Sundered Sea — and discovers the child is a living key to the seal binding the drowned god beneath the sea. Hunted by the crown's inquisitors and the child's original captors, Astrid gathers a ragged found family of exiles to reach the sunken throne before the thirteenth moon. There they learn their silent god was never gone but imprisoned inside the king, wearing his crown as a mask. In the climax, Astrid must choose between restoring their god's voice and freeing the king, and instead unbinds both by giving the god their own name, ending the silence at the cost of their sworn oath.
about_author: Wendell Marchetti is a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing shipwreck ledgers along a fog-bound coast before turning to fiction. He writes fantasy about oaths, salt, and the families people build when their gods stop answering.

chapters.title: The Child at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Astrid Ravensworth, mid-contract and weary of a god that no longer answers prayers, finds a mud-soaked child on their doorstep speaking a language older than any kingdom. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness cracking open a hardened heart.

chapters.title: What the Tide Remembers
chapters.summary: A scholar of dead tongues, Ysolde Fenwick, translates fragments of the child's speech: warnings about a seal beneath the Sundered Sea breaking with each turn of the moon. POV: Ysolde. Emotional beat: intellectual wonder curdling into dread as the countdown becomes real.

chapters.title: Inquisitors at Thornfell
chapters.summary: Crown inquisitors raid the mountain passes hunting 'the vessel,' forcing Astrid to burn a decade of smuggler contacts to get the child out alive. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: loyalty tested — old debts versus the new duty growing in their chest.

chapters.title: The Company of Broken Oaths
chapters.summary: Astrid assembles exiles: deserter Brannoc, disgraced priest Sera Ilva, and thief twins Pip and Wren. Around a fire, each confesses the oath that ruined them. POV: Brannoc. Emotional beat: strangers becoming something like family through shared failure.

chapters.title: Thirteen Moons, Twelve Gone
chapters.summary: The child, named Nell, begins dreaming the drowned god's memories — including one of Astrid's own god screaming behind a crown. The company realizes the enemy wears the king's face. POV: Nell. Emotional beat: terror and awe; innocence carrying unbearable knowledge.

chapters.title: The Road Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Guided by Nell's dreams, the company descends a smuggler road into flooded caverns where the sea has been seeping inland for centuries. An inquisitor ambush costs them Sera Ilva. POV: Pip. Emotional beat: grief sharpening resolve; the first true sacrifice.

chapters.title: Court of the Hollow King
chapters.summary: To reach the coast, the company infiltrates the capital and witnesses the king — hollow-eyed, reciting prayers in Nell's dead language — unknowingly feeding the thing on his throne. POV: Ysolde. Emotional beat: horror of complicity; the enemy is also a victim.

chapters.title: The Betrayal of Names
chapters.summary: Wren, offered restoration of her stolen name by the inquisitors, betrays the company's route — then returns, having learned the inquisitors serve the crowned thing itself. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: shame, forgiveness, and the theme that truth outweighs blind loyalty.

chapters.title: The Drowned Throne
chapters.summary: On the thirteenth moon, the company breaches the sunken throne room. Astrid confronts the crowned thing and finds their silent god imprisoned within it, begging for release through the king's mouth. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: the climactic choice between god, king, and self.

chapters.title: A Name Given Freely
chapters.summary: Astrid surrenders their own name to the god, unbinding it from the king and ending the silence — the god speaks its first word as Astrid's old life dissolves. The company sails home as family, Nell laughing in two living languages. POV: Nell. Emotional beat: bittersweet rebirth; identity remade through love rather than oath.
